basis: COMPUTED from the cycle mass flow and the sources below

sources.lambda_1atm: MEASURED: stoichiometric JP-10/air at 353 K, mean cell width 60.4 mm (39-84), Austin and Shepherd, Detonations in hydrocarbon fuel blends, Combust. Flame 132 (2003); kerosene vapour/air at 353 K about 60 mm in the same review literature
sources.lambda_scaling: PROJECTED: cell width taken inversely proportional to initial pressure and to the square root of initial temperature; Pintgen and Shepherd (ISABE-2005-1304) report partially oxidised kerosene/air cells of 22-24 mm at 1 atm and 3-9 mm at 6 atm (24-404 C), consistent with the inverse-pressure trend
sources.fill_height: MEASURED rule: critical fresh-mixture height h* = (12 +/- 5) cell widths, Bykovskii, Zhdan and Vedernikov, Continuous spin detonations, J. Propulsion Power 22(6) 2006, as restated in Zhou, Wu and Wang, Progress of continuously rotating detonation engines, Chinese J. Aeronautics 2016
sources.v_det: brief section 4.3: 1800-2000 m/s class; 1850 m/s used
sources.h2_credit: PROJECTED: the 10% hydrogen pilot energy is credited with a 15% smaller cell; Austin and Shepherd (2003) show hydrogen addition shrinking hydrocarbon cells, but give no number at this fraction and pressure

refusal.target: annular RDC whose channel holds its detonation cells inside the 272 mm envelope
refusal.computed: one wave in a 228.0 mm annulus needs 290.6 m/s fill (Mach 0.592) through a 4.98 mm channel, 0.53 cell widths
refusal.physics: with cells near 9.38 mm at the delivery pressure the fill height of 12 cells cannot be met at a subsonic fill velocity in a channel at least one cell wide; it fits once the cell is at most 4.83 mm, which needs more hydrogen or oxygen enrichment than the brief's 10% hydrogen energy
